slides.title: Competition Plays Out in the Open
bullets: Every active company in the therapeutic area is present and visible
Presentations, stands, satellite symposia generate competitive information
An MSL inevitably absorbs some of it during normal activity
The real question is not whether, but how to do it ethically

slides.title: Legitimate Intelligence Comes Only From Public Sources
bullets: Oral presentations, posters, and symposia open to the public
Materials freely distributed at stands
Official congress publications and abstracts
Taking notes on a public talk or openly stated booth messaging is fair game

slides.title: What Is Never Acceptable
bullets: Obtaining information through deception or hiding your affiliation
Accessing restricted materials or sessions without authorization
Posing as an HCP or unaffiliated attendee to enter a restricted symposium
Pressuring competitor stand staff, often junior, to reveal unpublished strategy

slides.title: Route Intelligence Through Formal Processes
bullets: Ethically gathered intelligence goes through a dedicated CI function
Not used informally or directly in HCP conversations
Informal comparative use risks unauthorized comparative communication
Many markets impose specific regulatory and compliance restrictions here

slides.title: Documentation Is a Compliance Safeguard
bullets: Governance frameworks require traceable capture
Record who captured the information, when, and from what public source
This improves the quality of aggregate competitive analysis
It also protects the organization in any later audit

slides.title: Discipline Protects the Value, Not Just the Rules
bullets: This discipline is not a limit on the value an MSL can add
It is what makes competitive intelligence sustainable and defensible
It stays coherent with Medical Affairs' reputation for integrity

takeaway.title: Competitive intelligence is only valuable if it is gathered ethically and used correctly
bullets: Public, open sources are the only legitimate origin for this information
Deception, restricted access, and pressure tactics are always off-limits
Formal CI channels and traceable documentation keep it defensible
